 1.

The challenge in this first appeal is to the award passed by  the reference Court dated 03.05.2008, by which, the reference Court has  awarded enhanced compensation to the amount of Rs. 3,75,875/- along  with solatium and the interest.
The LAR no. 334/1997, is impugned in the  this First Appeal.
2. The land of the present appellants / original claimants was  acquired for Nimna Dudhna Dam Project.

So far as land of the appellants  are concerned, it was in a field Survey No. 55, Village Kedarwakadi,
 admeasuring 04.85 HR and was Pot Kharab land.

sentences.text: While doing so, Hon'ble Apex Court disposed of the First Appeals in terms of order dated 07.02.2023 passed by the High Court in First Appeal No. 1351/2009 and connected matters.
The copy of order dated 25.02.2026, passed by Hon'ble Apex Court and produced by Advocate Mr. Kale, is taken on record.

The said order is reproduced as under :
 "1. Delay condoned.
 2. Leave granted.
 3. We have heard the learned counsel appearing for the  3 53FA453.2019.odt appellant(s) and the learned counsel appearing for the respondent(s).
4. Both the counsel appearing for the parties are in agreement that the decision rendered by the High Court dated 07.02.2023 in First Appeal No. 1351/2009 and connected matters, would govern the present appeal(s) as well.
5.

In the aforesaid decision dated 07.02.2023, the following order has been passed by the High Court :
"XXX (A) In all these appeals, respective appellants-claimants Vishwanath Babasaheb Kavale And Anr vs The State Of Mah And Ors on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23517475/
2 shall be entitled for the rate of compensation as agreed between themselves and the acquiring body, which is as follows :
Classification Rate Dry Lands Rs. 2400/- per are Semi-irrigated lands Rs. 3600/- per are Fully Irrigated Lands Rs. 4800/- per are Potkharab Lands Rs. 1200/- per are (B) The appellants-claimants shall also be entitled to get Interest under Sections 28 and 34 of the land Acquisition Act, 1894, from the respective dates of awards passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.

(C) The appellants-claimants shall be entitled to get interest @12% per annum as a special component from the date of Notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894, till the date of passing respective awards by the  4 53FA453.2019.odt  Special Land Acquisition Officer, as per Section 23 (1A) of  the Act.
(D) The appellants-claimants shall also be entitled to get  30% solatium on the difference of market value under Section 23(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
(E) The awards be modified accordingly.
(F) The appeals are accordingly disposed of.
No order as to  costs.
(G) Pending Civil Applications, if any, stand disposed of.

(H) Liberty to pay deficit Court fee, if any, within two weeks  after it is computed by the office.
 (I) Record and Proceedings be sent back to the Reference  Court."
 6.
Accordingly, all these appeal(s) are disposed of in  terms of the order dated 07.02.2023 passed by the High  Court in First Appeal No. 1351/2009 and connected matters.
However, the appellants shall not be entitled to any interest  for the period of delay.
7. Consequently, the impugned order passed by the High  Court dated 02.08.2022 is set aside."
4. Mr Kale, learned counsel thus submitted that the present claimants/present appellants are also entitled for the same rate.

sentences.text: He has produced that order on record.
He stated that order dated 15.12.2017, passed in Special Leave Petition (Civil) Diary No. 34448/2017, by the Hon'ble Apex Court is crystal clear.

He has tendered the copy of the order dated 15.12.2017, passed in SLP (Civil)
Diary No. 34448/2017, which is reproduced as under :
 "UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following  ORDER Delay condoned.
The special leave petitions are dismissed."
6. In the aforesaid background, I have gone through the record of the case.

Admittedly, by way of acquisition of land, the claimants are deprived of their property and, therefore, the pieces of the land were separately categorized and compensation was accordingly, paid based on the category determined by the reference Court.
Order passed by Hon'ble Apex Court dated 25.02.2026, is crystal clear and also governs issue involved in present case.

Hence, I am inclined to pass the following order:
6 53FA453.2019.odt ORDER i.
First Appeal is allowed.

ii. The claimants shall be entitled for the compensation for the nature of land which was decided by the reference Court i.e. if dry land Rs. 2400/-, if semi-irrigated land Rs. 3600/-, if fully irrigated land Rs. 4800/- and if Pot Kharab land Rs. 1200/-.

iii. The appellants shall be entitled to the interest under Sections 28 and 34 of the Land Acquisition Act as per the Full Bench Judgment of this Court in the case of State of Maharashtra Vs. Kailash Shiva Rangari, 2016 AIR (Bom.) 141.

v.

vi. The appellants shall pay deficit court fees.
vii. Award be drawn accordingly.
